The root cause of the incorrect result is in `lib_unicode_nfc.py`: `same_text` simply returns the boolean result of `left == right` — i.e., it does no normalization whatsoever. The `check.py` test uses the same Unicode code point (`'é'`) on both sides, so the equality holds and the assertion passes. There is no mismatch in the documented inputs; the utility behaves correctly on them.

DEFECT: lib_unicode_nfc.py::same_text | MECHANISM: the function performs no Unicode normalization, so `same_text` compares operands lexicographically rather than as equivalent Unicode sequences.
